recipes.title: Anime character atelier
inputs: Approved character reference, costume notes and target framing
Pose/depth guide and an editable repair mask
stages: Compare four base seeds with no optional style adapter
Lock design; add matched reference conditioning and pose guidance
Repair only a reviewed crop; preserve the original face and silhouette for comparison
Compare non-generative upscale with gentle tiled redraw
Export full image, masks, recipe and cropped contact sheet
acceptance: Line quality at final display size
recipes.stop: Stop before finishing when composition or identity is wrong.

recipes.title: Manga page with controlled panels
inputs: Panel layout, script and recurring-character references
stages: Author panel rectangles and reading order deterministically
Generate each panel with its own camera/pose control
Unify line weight and screentones in a layered canvas
Typeset balloons and sound effects as editable vector/text layers
Proofread at print and phone sizes
recipes.stop: Do not repeatedly regenerate a whole page to fix one balloon.

recipes.title: Fantasy scene from a 3D blockout
inputs: Simple scene blockout, camera and region masks
stages: Render neutral depth/normal guides from a deterministic scene
Explore material and lighting concepts with fixed geometry guides
Branch region edits for architecture, foliage and atmosphere
Composite protected geometry or labels from the source
Produce wide, portrait and mobile-safe crops
recipes.stop: Reject geometry drift before decorative detail.

recipes.title: Reference-faithful product assets
inputs: Actual product image or render; logo and protected-region mask
stages: Create lighting/background proposals without changing the approved product
Apply a bounded background or shadow edit
Composite original product pixels where exactness is required
Inspect silhouette, typography and reflections at 100 percent
Export campaign variants and editable source layers
recipes.stop: Never infer an unobserved product feature and present it as exact.

recipes.title: H3 staged seed laboratory
inputs: Approved first frame and a single-shot brief
stages: Validate one native short baseline in an isolated backend
Prepare complete prompt/reference conditioning once
Sample a bounded seed set with one matching preview schedule
Review motion and audio; approve a candidate explicitly
Render the final branch with its own recorded schedule and review again
recipes.stop: Do not upscale or extend an unapproved shot. A Turbo winner is not guaranteed to win a different schedule.

recipes.title: H3 multiframe and continuation bench
inputs: Accepted clip, anchor frames, timeline and immutable original audio
stages: Mark anchor frames with explicit time/frame coordinates
Create two short continuation proposals with overlap handles
Retain complete prefix context and compatible latent geometry
Inspect boundary motion, lighting, identity and audio before assembly
Join accepted shots with recorded editorial decisions
recipes.stop: Longer continuation must not silently replace the approved prefix.

recipes.title: H3 latent versus pixel finishing
inputs: One accepted low-resolution clip with original audio and conditioning
stages: Keep a no-redraw reference export
Branch learned latent enlargement plus model-native refinement
Branch independent video restoration from decoded frames
Use equal target resolution and inspect matching time/crop regions
Measure wall time, peak memory, temporal defects and accepted benefit
recipes.stop: Keep the simpler branch unless added detail survives blind review.

recipes.title: LTX-2.5 connected-shot study
inputs: A short shot list and reference identity pack
stages: Resolve the exact split model, new encoder and VAE bundle
Run the official distilled schedule unchanged as baseline
Compare single-shot assembly with native multishot
Add fidelity rendering only to an accepted candidate
Preserve audio, timestamps and all stage outputs
recipes.stop: Do not transplant LTX-2.3 encoders or arbitrary SDXL sampler defaults.

recipes.title: Authored motion into video
inputs: A Blender motion proxy, pose/depth frames and optional edit mask
stages: Start a separate supported Wan2.1-VACE baseline; do not conflate it with Wan2.2
Compare H3 control with the same authored motion and brief
Benchmark Wan2.2 I2V separately with its required noise-stage components
Add wrapper-only features only for a concrete missing capability
Select by motion fidelity and editing control, not prettiest unrelated demo
recipes.stop: Abort a branch when dependencies require altering the working AMD environment.

recipes.title: Image to usable 3D prop
inputs: Approved prop image, intended scale and target polygon/texture budget
stages: Benchmark shape and texture stages separately on a compatible worker
Inspect silhouette from unseen views and remove unintended floaters
Clean topology, UVs, material channels and LODs
Render a neutral turntable and light-rotation comparison
Export GLB and round-trip into Blender and the target engine
recipes.stop: A nice turntable does not certify topology, collision or riggability.

recipes.title: Rigged 3D to consistent sprite pack
inputs: Approved mesh or existing Lanternkeeper scene; frame/palette contract
stages: Use an authored rig or separately reviewed automatic rig proposal
Render contact, passing and recovery poses with fixed camera and pivot
Reduce with one shared palette and inspect silhouettes at target scale
Check foot contact, alpha fringe and duplicated frames
Pack atlas with anchors and durations; test actual engine playback
recipes.stop: Interpolation cannot invent correct missing gait poses.

recipes.title: Tileable material laboratory
inputs: Material brief, real-world scale and tile size
stages: Author a procedural base for repeatable structure
Use generation for optional visual variation, not physical measurement
Inspect 3x3 tiling and all PBR channels under changing light
Preserve neutral albedo separately from lighting
Export channel naming, color-space declarations and procedural source
recipes.stop: Do not accept a texture using only its beauty render.

recipes.title: Project-owned style and identity adapters
inputs: A recurring asset brief and rights-reviewed training/reference data
stages: Compare prompt-only and reference-conditioned baselines first
Choose one supported family; prepare captions and held-out views
Train an isolated small experiment with saved configuration
Compare zero, low and medium adapter strengths across held-out prompts
Retain the adapter only when useful output rate improves without identity/style leakage
recipes.stop: A larger adapter collection is not a substitute for a controlled test.

recipes.title: Editable audiovisual campaign assembly
inputs: Accepted images/clips, script, aspect ratios and rights-cleared audio
stages: Keep titles, captions, logos and transitions deterministic and editable
Use HyperFrames in Codex for HTML/GSAP composition after defining DESIGN.md
Mix optional generated music as a separate tracked asset
Render social variants without regenerating the accepted artwork
Review crop, caption timing, loudness and duration
recipes.stop: Do not bake changeable campaign text into an expensive generated video.
